executive_summary: L&T’s record order book and cash collection strengthen execution visibility, but the quality of the September profit matters more than the headline increase. Core PPM margins remain below the full-year target, while advanced customer payments produce unusually low net working capital and new technology investments create fresh allocation demands.
research_stance: Diversified execution franchise with substantial order visibility; assess margin conversion and capital allocation before extrapolating cash and profit growth.
results_analysis: September 2026 consolidated sales were ₹78,750.00 crore, +15.8% YoY and +15.9% QoQ. PAT was ₹5,949.00 crore, +27.2% YoY and +19.3% QoQ. These percentage changes use the rounded local dataset, so small differences from company-exact growth percentages are expected.

Local operating profit was ₹8,814.00 crore and OPM 11.00%, compared with 13.00% a year earlier and 12.00% in June 2026. PAT margin was 7.55%. OPM is the dataset’s operating-profit/sales measure, not automatically management-adjusted EBITDA or a segment EBIT margin.

Local net-profit ₹5,949 crore differs materially from the call’s group PAT approximately ₹5,200 crore. Profit before/after minority interests and other perimeter definitions may explain this, but the report does not assume a fully reconciled attribution bridge. Call group EBITDA 8.7% and PPM EBITDA 7.0% also differ from the local operating-profit ₹8,814 crore/rounded 11% series, particularly with financial-services interest accounting. Keep verification pending for these headline comparisons.

FY26 annual CFO was ₹16,741 crore and free cash flow ₹12,272 crore. These are annual figures, not September-quarter cash flow. Latest balance-sheet borrowings were ₹140,300 crore at 2026-09-30; gross borrowings must not be confused with call net debt. Snapshot ROCE 14.60% is an older-period return measure, not a freshly recomputed quarterly return.

thesis_drivers.title: Record backlog improves visibility
thesis_drivers.evidence: Order inflow ₹1.48 trillion was +28% YoY; order book ₹8.54 trillion was +28% with average 33-month execution. The book is 54% international and 73% of the international book is Middle East, creating both scale and regional concentration.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

thesis_drivers.title: Execution is broadening but core margins lag
thesis_drivers.evidence: PPM revenue grew 20% YoY, while its EBITDA margin 7.0% was down 30 bp. Water project costs, supply chain pressure and young projects below profit recognition thresholds must normalize for 7.8% FY27 PPM guidance.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

thesis_drivers.title: Collections materially improve liquidity
thesis_drivers.evidence: NWC 1.7% is a record low versus 4.1% March. It benefits from customer advances; management expects below the old 10% year-end guide, not necessarily 1.7% permanently.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

thesis_drivers.title: Portfolio reshaping offers optionality with risk
thesis_drivers.evidence: Hyderabad Metro exit now targets December 31 rather than September 30. AI compute, data-center and semiconductor investments should be judged by contracted cash returns; planned >10,000 NVIDIA B300 GPUs are capacity commitments, not equity value by default.
thesis_drivers.source: September 2026 local financials and current company earnings-call transcript; source links below

claim_audit.claim: September 2026 local consolidated revenue ₹78,750.00 crore, operating profit ₹8,814.00 crore and PAT ₹5,949.00 crore.
claim_audit.assessment: Re-read the current parquet and compared the report inputs. This verifies the report against its stated local data source; company-adjusted and attributable measures require the separate call/filing bridge below.

claim_audit.claim: FY26 operating cash flow ₹16,741 crore and dataset free cash flow ₹12,272 crore.
claim_audit.assessment: Annual cash flow was checked against the current cash-flow table. This is FY ended March 2026, not September-quarter cash flow; investing-flow and capex definitions must not be silently interchanged.

The generic financial-table funding field was re-read. It is not automatically equivalent to industrial net debt or to debt excluding leases; explicit company-specific bridges are recorded where available.

claim_audit.assessment: The backlog is a current execution pipeline, not committed shareholder cash receipts.

claim_audit.assessment: The combination implies about39% of total backlog is Middle East exposure—analyst multiplication, not a separately disclosed total-share figure.
An average is not a fixed maturity schedule or a guarantee that all work converts in33months.

claim_audit.assessment: Neither figure is interchangeable with local generic11% OPM. Group financial-services accounting also complicates generic interest/expense classifications.

claim_audit.assessment: ₹52billion is₹5,200cr. The₹749cr gap remains unreconciled; the report must not invent a minority-interest explanation as a confirmed bridge.

business_economics: Backlog quality depends on mix, execution age, contract price protection, certification and customer funding. A33-month average conversion period gives visibility but does not eliminate project delays, scope changes or cash-collection risk. The growing energy/international mix differs from the domestic infrastructure portfolio.

About54% of backlog was international and73% of that portfolio was Middle East; multiplying these gives roughly39% of the total. This is an analyst concentration estimate. It highlights logistics, counterparty and geopolitical exposure even though customer advances can improve near-term working capital.
earnings_quality: The report retains local₹5,949cr net profit and management₹5,200cr group PAT as distinct, unreconciled definitions. It does not call one attributable PAT without the actual attribution statement. Likewise, group8.7% EBITDA, PPM7% margin and local11% OPM must remain separate series.

Treasury income benefits from the release of working capital, while the net working-capital ratio benefits from customer advances. These are real cash advantages when collected, but they should not be extrapolated as permanent operating margin or an endlessly repeatable cash inflow. Gross working capital remains a separate exposure.
capital_allocation: The established EPC/manufacturing portfolio, listed financial/technology interests and new compute/semiconductor platforms need separate capital and liability bridges. A SOTP that deducts all group borrowings from industrial EBITDA value can misclassify financial-services funding and double-count subsidiary interests.

The AI compute disclosure is more concrete than an optional thematic mention: around$750m investment and>10,000GPUs with a significant portion contracted. The return case still needs power/hosting costs, utilization, obsolescence, contract duration and funding. The Hyderabad Metro exit delay also matters because expected capital release may not arrive on the original timetable.
valuation_logic: Start with core PPM earnings under the7.8% FY27 margin target, then add listed/unlisted interests and deduct appropriate parent-level liabilities and holding-company costs. Newplatforms require their own cash-flow model rather than a narrative premium on the EPC multiple.

The bull case requires backlog conversion, margin recovery and successful capital recycling; the base case lets advances normalize and commits full capital to new platforms; the bear case combines weak margins, cash reversal and delayed disposals. Exact fair value is withheld until PAT attribution and group-debt perimeters reconcile.
peer_positioning: Cemindia and NCC are narrower project-execution comparisons; BHEL and capital-goods manufacturers have different manufacturing/order cycles. Listed subsidiaries should be benchmarked in their own industries. L&T’s consolidated multiple is not directly comparable with a pure EPC company’s multiple.
